verdict.rationale: mParticle documents Warehouse Sync, which ingests existing tables from Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery and Databricks into mParticle via an API, SQL reference and data mapping. Audiences built in mParticle can then be connected to audience outputs for activation. However, the evidence shows data being copied into mParticle rather than models and audiences being defined in place on warehouse tables. The 'Composable Audiences' page appears only as a title, with no supporting content. missing for 10: documented in-warehouse model and audience definition without ingesting into mParticle, content for Composable Audiences, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can run warehouse-native: define models and audiences on tables already in my warehouse and activate them without re-collecting the data (reverse ETL)

citations.quote: Warehouse Sync ingests data from your own warehouse into mParticle
Once you have created an audience, you must connect it to an audience output where you can activate it.
